Section 5 • \(\xi\)1D

5.3 From per-sample to ensemble estimates: ergodicity and averaging over sightlines

Suppose we have \(N\) realizations \(\{\delta_i^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda)\}_{s=1}^{N}\) for a fixed sightline \(\vec{x}_{\perp}\). A natural estimator of the ensemble 2PCF at spectral separation \(\Delta\) is then the average of the per-sample estimators: \begin{equation} \widehat{\xi}_{ij}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Delta\right) \;\equiv\; \frac{1}{N}\sum_{s=1}^{N} \widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Delta\right), \tag{5.9} \end{equation} where \(\widehat{\xi}_{ij}^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Delta)\) is given by Eq. (5.2).

Interactive

Under mild regularity conditions, these empirical estimators converge to the corresponding ensemble quantity as the number of independent realizations and/or sampled sightlines increases. In many cosmological applications, however, one effectively has access only to a few realizations of the underlying random process. In that context, one often invokes an ergodic assumption: ensemble averages may be approximated by averages over a sufficiently large available domain, here represented by the spectral coordinate \(\Lambda\), and possibly also by averaging over many sightlines.

Particularizing Eq. (4.2) for \(L=2 \longrightarrow \mathcal{C} = C_{12}\) we can regroup terms to obtain: \begin{align} &\xi\!\left(\Lambda_\alpha,\Lambda_\beta\right) \;\equiv\; \Big\langle \delta^{(s)}\left(\Lambda_\alpha\right)\, \delta^{(s)}(\Lambda_\beta) \Big\rangle_{\rm ens} \;=\; \int_{\Omega}\! d\mathbb P(\omega)\; \delta\left(\Lambda_\alpha,\omega\right)\, \delta\left(\Lambda_\beta,\omega\right) \; = \notag \\ &= \frac{1}{ \bigl[1+\TextZero{C_{12}(\Lambda_\alpha)}\bigr] \bigl[1+\TextZero{C_{12}(\Lambda_\beta)}\bigr] } \Bigg[ - \TextZero{C_{12}(\Lambda_\alpha)\,C_{12}(\Lambda_\beta)} + \TextTwo{\xi_{11}(\Lambda_\alpha,\Lambda_\beta)} + \TextTwo{\xi_{22}(\Lambda_\alpha,\Lambda_\beta)} + \TextTwo{\xi_{12,\mathrm{sym}}(\Lambda_\alpha,\Lambda_\beta)} + \notag\\[0.6em] &\qquad + \TextThree{\xi_{1(12), \mathrm{sym}}(\Lambda_\alpha,\Lambda_\beta)} + \TextThree{\xi_{2(12), \mathrm{sym}}(\Lambda_\alpha,\Lambda_\beta)} + \TextFour{\xi_{(12)(12)}(\Lambda_\alpha,\Lambda_\beta)} \Bigg]. \tag{5.10} \end{align}
